110449=Tile Management Rules
110451=Declaring War\n1. Attacking a city requires the Alliance Leader or an R4 to declare war. \n2. Each alliance can declare war once a day and only on one city at a time. \n3. An alliance must have more than 20 members to declare war. \n4. The war lasts for 12 hours, during which alliance members can attack the city. Multiple alliances can declare war on the same city. \nAttacking Cities\n1. The city has NPC defenders that survivors must defeat first; if not defeated quickly, the defenders will recover all HP. \n2. After defeating all defenders, survivors must demolish the city's durability. Troops can initiate demolitions periodically. The city's durability will slowly restore over time, so it's recommended to gather enough survivors for a concentrated attack. \n3. After demolishing all durability, the ownership of the city is determined based on the points obtained by participating alliances (Points = number of defenders killed * defender points + durability demolished * durability points). \nNote: During the demolishment stage, only durability destruction counts toward siege points. Winning the siege itself does not grant additional points. \n\nOccupation Rules\n1. A Level 1 city must be occupied first (the first Level 1 city doesn't need to follow adjacent rules); thereafter, any city your alliance declares war on must be adjacent to your alliance's existing territory.

302062=Champion Duel\n Sign-up\n1. Sign-up: Monday to Tuesday. Combat will not result in losses. Heroes and units regular usage will not be affected. \n2. The event is divided into 3 stages: Qualifier, Knockout, and Championship. Top 64 of the Qualifier stage will enter the Knockout stage, and Top 8 emerging from the Knockout stage will enter the Championship stage. \n3. Troop formations can be changed in "My Troop Formation" before the match starts. \n\nQualifier \n1. Wednesday is when the In-State Qualifier begins; a total of 10 rounds of combats will ensue, with an interval of 60 Minutes in between. \n2. Survivors can change troop formations anytime and apply the latest formation to the next match. There will be a 5-minute cooldown before another change. Formations cannot be changed 5 Minutes before each match starts. \n3. 3 accumulated losses will be deemed eliminated. \n4. Top 64 determined by the number of victories will advance to the Knockout stage. (If it's a Cross-State duel, then the Top 64 come from top 32 of both servers.)\n5. When two survivors have the same victory number, the survivor with more points (determined by combat loss) will be deemed eligible for the next stage competition. \n\nKnockout \n1. Thursday is when the Knockout starts. \n2. Top 64 of the Qualifier stage will be divided into 8 groups for the Knockout competition. \n3. There are 3 rounds of matches in the Knockout stage, with an interval of 1 hour in between. After 3 rounds of competition, 1 survivor will advance from each group to enter the final Championship. \n\nChampionship \n1. Top 8 of the Knockout will enter the Championship stage. \n2. Survivors can change troop formations anytime and apply the latest formation to the next match. There will be a 5-minute cooldown before another change. Formations cannot be changed 15 Minutes before each match starts. \n3. Championship includes Quarterfinals, Semi-finals, and Finals, which start at 12:00 (Apocalypse Time) Friday, Saturday, and Sunday respectively. \n4. Multiple rounds of combat will ensue, and survivors with more victories will advance. \n\n Combat Attributes\n1. During the event, bonuses to siege attacks and to siege defenses are excluded. \n2. All techs related to combat bonuses will be effective. \n3. During the event, if a survivor's hero stats are enhanced (i.e. hero upgraded, skill unlocked), tech advanced, structure upgraded or other similar improvements made, then the survivor must go to "My Lineup" to save the change in order to make it work on the next match. \n\nRewards\n1. In the Qualifier, a reward can be earned for each victory. The unclaimed rewards will be sent via mail after the entire event is over. \n2. In the Knockout and Championship competitions, all survivors will receive rewards based on their ranking. \n3. Knockout and Championship competition rewards will be sent via mail after the event is over.

Upon the beginning of the Apocalypse Clash Season, City ownership of the entire apocalyptic continent will be reset, and Survivor's headquarters will re-land on the continent. \n2. 302845=Clash for Glory
302846=Upon the beginning of the event, an alliance can declare war on another one. \nThe alliance that is declared war upon cannot refuse to fight. \nThe event is divided into 2 phases: the Prep phase and the Battle phase. Alliances can obtain Glory Points by destroying the rival's Alliance Centers and season buildings. \nWhen the event ends, the alliance with higher Glory Points is deemed victory, and the winning alliance will grab 20% Season Points from the losing alliance. \nDuring the event, if one side's Alliance Center Ⅰ is destroyed, then that side is deemed defeated.
302847=Alliance Center
302848=Alliance Centers are essential for placing season buildings, so prioritize constructing them. \nThe Alliance Leader and R4 members are allowed to place down Alliance Centers. \nEach alliance can build up to 3 Alliance Centers, which must be placed on different levels of tiles. \nOnce placed, you can send troops to garrison the center and accelerate its construction. \nAfter recalling, the Alliance Center's durability will be emptied. Construction resources will be spent again to place it next time.
302849=Season Buildings
302850=Survivors can build their own season buildings to enjoy rich season stat bonuses. \nSeason buildings must be placed near corresponding Alliance Centers. \nSapphire and Sandsoul tiles on the world map generate sustainable resources once captured. These resources are used for constructing and upgrading season buildings. \nRecalled season buildings will be in cooldown before they can be placed down again.
302851=Capture Tiles

If survivors lack sufficient virus resistance, their troops' attack ability will significantly decrease. \nVirus Lab can boost the resistance, making it easier to capture tiles. \nLand Office increases the number of tiles we can control.

376029=Gameplay
376030=1. The two matched alliances will enter the Canyon to engage in battle. \n2. On the battlefield, your <color=#b13737>units will not perish</color>, and all <color=#b13737>injured units will recover for free</color> after battle ends. \n3. A <color=#b13737>free teleporting chance</color> is available every 3 minutes on the battlefield, with no need for all troops to return to Headquarters. \n4. Initial or sustained occupation of buildings will contribute to Alliance Points, and the alliance with higher points wins. \n5. Capturing buildings, beating opposing survivors, and gathering stones will earn Personal Points. \n6. Escorting Energy Cells to the Alliance Beacon will reward massive Alliance and Personal Points. \n7. Defeating the Canyon Captain grants buffs to all allied members. \n8. After the battle period ends, the side with higher Alliance Points will claim victory. Survivors will receive generous rewards based on Personal Points and the alliance's outcome.
376031=Schedule
376032=Phase Overview \n1. Voting is open from Mondays to Tuesdays, with Wednesday for registration, Thursday for matchmaking, and Friday for combat. \n2. Alliances ranked in the <color=#b13737>Top 20</color> by power and population <color=#b13737>reaching 40</color> can register for the event. \n3. The alliance leader and R4 members can register for the alliance. \n4. Survivors must have been in the alliance for at least 24 hours to participate in the event. \n5. An alliance must have <color=#b13737>at least 15 registerers</color> to join the matchmaking. \n6. Team 2 Info\n· Team 2 registration opens 2 weeks after Canyon Clash begins.\n· Cannot register for this week's Team 2 if current alliance active members are <60.\n· Cannot register for this week's Team 2 if last week, fewer than 20 survivors scored above 2,000 in a single Canyon battle. \n\nParticipants\n1. The alliance leader and R4 members can select Starters, Substitutes and Commanders on the Participants interface. \n2. There can be <color=#b13737>20</color> Starters, <color=#b13737>20</color> Substitutes, and <color=#b13737>2</color> Commanders. \n3. Members who have been offline for over 5 days are ineligible for battle or reserve selection. \n4. Only Starters and Substitutes can serve as Commanders. \n5. <color=#b13737>Each member can only participate in one team (including Starters and Substitutes).</color> \n\nEnter Battlefield\n1. Starters can enter the battlefield during the prep phase. \n2. If there are absent Starters, Substitutes can enter the battlefield when combat begins. \n3. When entering the battlefield, <color=#b13737>survivors must ensure that all troops are back to headquarters</color>, with all deployable units carried. \n\nBattle Start\n1. Prep Phase: Starters enter the battlefield and wait for combat to begin. \n2. Battle Phase: \n· Phase Ⅰ: Field Hospital and Water Refinery are accessible. Capturing them grants battlefield buffs, alliance points, and personal points. Capturing Quarry earns additional personal points. \n· Phase Ⅱ: Canyon Captain spawns. Alliance dealing higher damage to the Canyon Captain gains powerful battlefield buffs after defeating it. \n· Phase Ⅲ: Military Base opens. Capturing it grants many alliance points and personal points, as well as boosting your side's strengths. \n· Phase Ⅳ: Energy Station generates Energy Cells. Sending troops to capture and transport them to the Alliance Beacon will instantly grant massive battlefield points. \n\n3. Battle Over: The alliance with higher battlefield points wins. \n\n4. Injury Treatment: Injuries from the Canyon Clash will automatically heal after the battle ends. \n\n5. Reward Distribution: Both personal and alliance rewards will be sent via mail after the event. \n\n6. Commander System: \n· Commanders can be assigned during the registration phase, and allow for adjustments before the battlefield is accessible. Once accessible, Commanders can only be adjusted inside the battlefield. \n· Commanders can group the participants. \n· Commanders can issue commands on the battlefield, and guide actions. \n· Only R4/R5 can change Commander assignment.
376033=Both alliances respectively spawn in the upper-left and lower-right corners (Red and Blue zones) of the map, where fierce combat shall take place.
376034=Capturing the Field Hospital provides healing support, boosting injury healing speed and significantly lowering healing costs for battlefield combatants. The effect of multiple Field Hospitals stacks.
376035=Occupying the Military Base boosts the overall combat effectiveness of your side, enhancing both attack and defense, which is key to achieving battlefield victory. The effect of multiple Military Bases stacks.
376036=The Energy Station produces an Energy Cell at the 20-minute and 30-minute intervals. Both sides can send troops to capture the Energy Cells. The movement speed of the troop carrying the item will be reduced by 50%. Transporting the Energy Cell to the Alliance Beacon grants 100,000 alliance points to your side.

457530=[Rules] \n1. Each survivor can conduct up to 4 intercity trades per day. Each trade will occupy a truck for a certain period. The more squads unlocked, the more trucks available. \n2. Upon departure, the truck will follow a random route. During the trip, the truck could be plundered. No unit losses in the truck plunder, and each truck can be plundered twice at most. \n3. When the truck reaches its destination, the trade initiator can collect its remaining rewards. \n\n[Initiate Trade] \n1. Up to 5 heroes can be selected to protect a truck, and each hero can protect only 1 truck at a time. \n2. Once a truck departs, the defense heroes cannot be changed. \n3. Each truck has 1 free chance to change rewards during the selection phase. \n\n[Trade Rewards] \n1. After a truck reaches its destination, the remaining cargo on the truck can be collected. \n2. Keeping using Trade Contracts to switch trucks will increase the chances of obtaining high-quality trucks. \n3. Truck quality and the survivor's headquarters level determine the base value of truck cargo. \n4. The more cities captured by the survivor's alliance, the more cargo the truck can transport additionally, up to 7 extra cargo per truck. \n5. The higher the level of cities captured by the survivor's alliance, the greater the value of additional cargo. \n\n[Plunder Trucks]\n1. Survivors can loot non-allied trucks on the map up to 4 times daily. \n2. Upon victory, the attacker can plunder random cargo and resources from the truck, and reduce the truck's integrity by a certain percentage. \n3. Failed plunder does not consume plunder chances. \n4. Trucks with integrity below 50% cannot be further plundered. \n5. No unit losses in the truck plunder, and each truck can be plundered twice at most. \n\n[Probabilities] \n1. The spawning probabilities of trucks with different qualities based on the number of refreshes (including free refreshes) are listed as follows: \n(1st Refresh): D-grade (50%), C-grade (30%), B-grade (10%), A-grade (5%), S-grade (5%)\n(2nd Refresh): D-grade (30%), C-grade (30%), B-grade (20%), A-grade (10%), S-grade (10%)\n(3rd Refresh): D-grade (20%), C-grade (20%), B-grade (30%), A-grade (15%), S-grade (15%)\n(4th Refresh): D-grade (0%), C-grade (20%), B-grade (40%), A-grade (20%), S-grade (20%)\n(5th Refresh): D-grade (0%), C-grade (0%), B-grade (50%), A-grade (25%), S-grade (25%)\n(>5th Refresh): D-grade (0%), C-grade (0%), B-grade (0%), A-grade (0%), S-grade (100%)

Only the top 20 alliances in the State can get free regular trucks. \n\n[Truck Acquisition] \n1. Regular Truck: Eeverday at 00:00 State Time, alliances that meet the "Participation Requirements" will be granted a trade truck, and the truck won't enter the prep status until an R4/R5 assigns the truck commander. \n2. Express Truck: When there are no trucks in preparation, you can summon an Express Truck and automatically become the truck commander. \n\n[Truck Prep Phase] \n1. The prep phase lasts for 4 hours, after which the truck will automatically depart for various cities to conduct trade. \n2. Truck Commander: During the prep phase, the truck commander needs to assign escorts to the truck and confirm the cargo to be transported. \n3. Passengers: During the prep phase, passengers need to queue in front of the carriage they wish to board. At the end of the phase, one passenger will be randomly selected from the queue to enter the carriage. \n\n[Truck Travels] \n1. The truck could be attacked by other survivors when traveling, and 3 random slots of cargo will be looted when the attacker wins. \n2. Each truck can be looted up to 3 times. \n\n[Rewards] \n1. Truck Commander: Upon arrival, the truck commander will receive all remaining cargo rewards from the tractor and carriages. \n2. Passengers: Upon arrival, passengers will receive remaining cargo rewards from the carriages.

477845=Migration Phases
477846=Migration is divided into three phases: \n\nPhase Ⅰ: Prep Phase \nIn this phase, survivors can view Available States and contact the Presidents of desired destinations. \n\nPhase Ⅱ: Invitation Phase \nIn this phase, the President can invite survivors from other States. \nImmigration identity is determined based on Migration Score: Regular, Intermediate, Advanced, and Elite. Each identity type has a separate immigration quota. \n\nPhase Ⅲ: Free Migration \nIn this phase, survivors with Regular identity can freely immigrate to States that still have available Regular slots. Survivors with other identities cannot migrate freely; instead, they can only migrate when invited by other States. \n\nNote: During Phase Ⅱ & Ⅲ, Elite, Advanced, and Intermediate survivors may submit Special Immigration Applications. Once approved by the destination State's President, immigration will be allowed. \nInvitations and applications expire after 24 hours. If rejected, another invitation/application cannot be sent for 20 minutes. \n\nMigration Cooldown: After each successful migration, cannot migrate again for 30 days. \n\nState Rating: At the start of each migration event, some states will automatically adjust to [Fully Open] or [Semi-Open] status. Adjustments are based on recent migration scores of active survivors in the State. Semi-Open states will have reduced total migration slots, while Fully Open states will have increased slots.
477847=\nMigration Conditions: \nSurvivors may immigrate to a target State (if identity quota is available) only if all the following conditions are met: \n1. Have received an invitation, or hold a Regular identity during the Free Migration Phase. \n2. Headquarters meets the required level. \n3. The headquarters is not in combat and has no outgoing troops. \n4. Not the President of any State. \n5. Have not migrated during this event round. \n6. Not part of any Alliance.

510182=Event Overview \nThe Cross-State Capital Clash is a 1v1 competition between States, where the winner is determined by capturing the rival's Capital. \n4–8 States are matched into a group for a 2–3 week battle until a champion State is crowned! \nBecoming the champion is no easy feat-it takes the President's leadership to unite all the state forces! \n\nEvent Rules \nStates within a group are matched randomly, and the winning State advances to the next round, facing other winners until a champion is crowned. \nMatching Rules: Winners are matched with winners, and losers are matched with losers. Victory is achieved by capturing the enemy State's Capital. \n\nEvent Phases \nSunday to Friday: States compete for points by winning in various events to increase their state score. \nInvaders and Defenders: At the end of Friday Apocalypse Time, the side with the higher state score becomes the invader, and the lower-scoring side becomes the defender. \n\nCapital Clash\nStarting Saturday, the invader can teleport to the defender's state to attack their capital and contest ownership. The rules for cross-state capital contests follow the same format: during the contest period, the state that reaches 100% progress successfully captures the capital. If no state succeeds in capturing the capital by the end of the contest period, the capital belongs to the state with the highest capture progress. \n\nIf the invader wins, 2 new official positions will be granted. \nOnce the capital is captured, many diamond mines will spawn within its range, and only the winning side can gather them. \nFor survivors within the same state, unity and cooperation are essential!

Defeating <color=#f07100>1</color> enemy unit grants <color=#f07100>1</color> Glory Point & <color=#f07100>150</color> Personal Contribution Points. \n\n<color=#f07100>Victory and Defeat Criteria</color>\n1. 332219=Rules
332220=1. Feast Hosting: \n1.1 Top <color=#f07100>10</color> alliances can host the Feast after this event ends. \n1.2 There are three feast levels: <color=#f07100>Feast Grounds</color>, <color=#f07100>Flavor Fest</color>, and <color=#f07100>Yummy Stand</color>. Higher-ranked alliances can host higher-level feasts. The alliance ranked 1st is eligible for <color=#f07100>Feast Grounds</color>, alliances ranked 2-3 for <color=#f07100>Flavor Fest</color>, and alliances ranked 4-10 for <color=#f07100>>Yummy Stand</color>. \n1.3 Each qualified alliance can only host one feast. Once the feast starts, it will last for 1 hour and cannot be canceled. \n\n2. Participation Qualifications: \n2.1 To participate in the feast, you must be with an alliance that <color=#f07100>qualifies for hosting the feast</color>, and you can only join the feast hosted by that alliance. \n2.2 If you leave the alliance during the feast, you can still participate as long as you rejoin the same alliance before the settlement phase. \n\n3. Feast Schedule: \n3.1 Feast Building Placement: When the feast starts, alliance <color=#f07100>R5/R4</color> must build the feast building before hosting the feast. \n3.2 Serving Table: When the feast starts, tables will be arranged around the feast building at regular intervals. The quality of the tables includes Rustic, Standard, Premium, and Deluxe. Higher-level feasts will have better-quality tables.

910102=Event Rules: \n1. During the Arctic Ice Pit event, contests for Level 1, 2, and 3 ice pits start at <color=#c8212d>Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays 11:00:00</color> Apocalypse Time respectively, each lasting for 1 hour. \n2. The Ice Pit Clash takes place in your Home State during the first week of the event, and cross-State clashes in the same season grouping afterward. \n3. At the start of the clash, alliance members need to defeat the Tundra Titan together. Once defeated, the alliance with the highest damage points gains control of the corresponding Ice Pit. \n4. When the Alliance gains control of the Ice Pit, all members who <color=#c8212d>deal damage to the Tundra Titan</color> receive a participation reward. \n5. Teleporting your Headquarters to the area near the Ice Pit grants a 3× damage points bonus, but you may be attacked by other survivors. \n6. If the Tundra Titan is not defeated within the time limit, the Ice Pit re-enters a frozen state.\nFishing and Index: \n1. Once the ice pit is captured, all survivors in the same season grouping can use [Common Fishing Permits] or [Master Fishing Permits] to fish at the pit. \n2. Fishing yields index entries. Reaching collection milestones grants corresponding rewards. \n3. Surplus fish entries may be gifted to others to help complete collections and earn grand prizes! \n\nIce Pit Yields: \n1. The capturing survivor receives ice pit capture reward, and alliance members who contribute points receive a participation reward. \n2. Fishing in the ice pit captured by your alliance significantly increases chances for rare fish entries. \n3. When the total number of Fishing Permits collected in the Ice Pit reaches <color=#f07100>{0}</color>, the pit owner will receive a Fishing Red Packet worth <color=#f07100>{1}</color> Diamonds-ready to share with their allies!

1000007=Contest Rules:\n\n1. Once the event starts, contests for Lv.1/2/3 Trade Hubs begin at 11:00:00 (Apocalypse Time) on Mondays/Wednesdays/Fridays, lasting 1 hour each. \n2. The first week's contests occur within your home state; subsequent rounds are cross-state contests. During cross-state contests, you cannot attack Headquarters from other states outside the Trade Hub area. \n3. Ownership of Trade Hub is individual. Troops from the same alliance do not combat each other within the Hub, but <color=#cf1c20>their capture progress is calculated independently</color>. \n4. When your Headquarters is outside the Trade Hub area, the minimum capture time is 15 minutes. After relocating your Headquarters into the Trade Hub area, <color=#cf1c20>the minimum capture time reduces to 10 minutes</color>-but be warned, after moving in, <color=#cf1c20>you may suffer attacks from other survivors!</color> \n5. If the Trade Hub is unowned, the survivor with the highest capture progress when the contest ends becomes the Owner. If the Hub had an existing owner and no survivor reaches 100% capture progress by the end of the contest, the existing owner retains control. \n6. After ownership of a Trade Hub is confirmed, all alliance members who contributed capture progress at that hub will receive a participation reward. \n\nHub Shop Rules:\n\n1. After the contest, the Trade Hub Owner can tap the 'Stock' button to fully replenish the shop's shelves for the week. Alliance members get early access to purchase items. \n2. [Exclusive] items can only be purchased by the owner. The owner's allies enjoy discounted prices on purchasable items. \n3. When the owner chooses to open trade to the public, all survivors within the same season group can use Diamonds to purchase items. \n4. Each item in the Trade Hub Shop can only be purchased once before the next contest opens-first-come-first-served. The total daily purchase attempts for the entire shop are limited. \n5. Daily purchase attempts reset at 11:00:00 (Apocalypse Time).\n\nTax Rules:\n\n1. After each Trade Hub Contest ends, it enters a new contest phase. A portion of Diamonds earned from successful sales in the Hub Shop during the previous owner's tenure is converted into tax revenue. \n2. When all items in the shop are sold out or the owner steps down, taxes are granted as bonus red packets, allowing the owner to distribute them to alliance members via the chat channel.

1000024=Rules: \n\n1. The main rules are essentially the same as those in the Trade Hub event of the Dinosaur · Origin season. \n2. <color=#cf1c20>New [Night Market] mechanism</color>: When night falls, the shop refreshes with items unique to the Night Market. Survivors can use [Moon Tokens] to purchase these items. The daily purchase limits for Night Market items and daytime items are independent of each other. \n3. <color=#cf1c20>New [Moon Token Dividend Packs]</color>: Moon Tokens spent in the Trade Hub's Night Market will be converted into [Moon Token Dividend Packs] based on the tax rate before the next contest begins. These packs are given to the Trade Hub Owner, who can distribute them to the alliance. Members who claim them receive a random amount of Moon Tokens. \n\nContest Rules: \n\n1. Once the event starts, contests for Lv.1/2/3 Trade Hubs begin at 11:00:00 (Apocalypse Time) on Monday/Wednesday/Friday, lasting for 1 hour each. \n2. The first week's contests occur within your home state; subsequent rounds are cross-state contests. During cross-state contests, you cannot attack Headquarters from other states outside the Trade Hub area. \n3. Ownership of Trade Hubs is individual. Troops from the same alliance do not combat each other within the Hub, but their capture progress is calculated independently. \n4. When your Headquarters is outside the Trade Hub area, the minimum capture time is 15 minutes. After relocating your Headquarters into the Trade Hub area, the minimum capture time reduces to 10 minutes-but be warned, after teleporting in, you may suffer attacks from other survivors! \n5. If the Trade Hub is unowned, the survivor with the highest capture progress when the contest ends becomes the Owner. If the Hub had an existing owner and no survivor reaches 100% capture progress by the end of the contest, the existing owner retains control. \n6. After ownership of a Trade Hub is confirmed, all alliance members who contributed capture progress at that hub will receive a participation reward. \n\nTrade Hub Shop Rules: \n\n1. After the contest, the Trade Hub Owner can tap the <Stock> button to fully replenish the shop's shelves for the week. Alliance members get early access to purchase items. \n2. This season, the Trade Hub has a new [Night Market] mechanism. When night falls, the shop refreshes with items that can only be purchased during the night, using [Moon Tokens]. When night ends, these items are temporarily hidden, and the shop continues selling daytime items until the next night falls. \n3. [Exclusive] items can only be purchased by the Owner. The Owner's allies enjoy discounted prices on purchasable items. \n4. When the Owner chooses to open the shop, all survivors within the same season grouping can use Diamonds to purchase items in the daytime shop and Moon Tokens to purchase items in the Night Market. \n5. During both daytime and nighttime, each item in the Trade Hub can only be purchased once before the next contest opens-first come, first served. The daytime shop and the Night Market each have independent daily purchase limits. \n6. Daily purchase attempts reset at 11:00:00 (Apocalypse Time). \n\nTax Rules:\n\n1. After each Trade Hub Contest ends, it enters a new contest phase. A portion of Diamonds and Moon Tokens earned from successful sales in the Hub Shop during the previous owner's tenure is converted into tax revenue. \n2. When all items in the shop are sold out, or the Owner steps down, these taxes are distributed to the Owner as tax dividend. Diamond taxes are converted into Trade Dividend Packs, and Moon Token taxes are converted into Moon Token Dividend Packs. The Owner can distribute them to alliance members in the chat channel.\n3. Alliance members who claim Trade Dividend Packs receive varying amounts of Diamonds; those who claim Moon Token Dividend Packs receive varying amounts of Moon Tokens.

915189=<color=#354252>Phase Overview\n1. Publicity</color> \nDay 1 marks the publicity phase, during which the groupings for the current event will be revealed. \n<color=#354252>2. Comms</color> \nOn Day 2, the comms phase begins. Presidents of already grouped states may negotiate potential partnerships with ungrouped states. \n<color=#354252>3. Invitation</color> \nDays 3–4 mark the Invitation Phase. Presidents of grouped states can officially invite ungrouped states to join their camp and fight together. \n<color=#354252>4. System Allocation</color> \nAfter the invitation phase ends, the system will automatically and randomly allocate any states that were not successfully grouped. \n<color=#354252>5. Battle Prep</color> \nDay 5 is the battle prep phase, during which survivors can share tactics and strategize. \n<color=#354252>6. Battle</color> \nDay 6 is the battle phase. Battle begins at 12:00 Apocalypse Time and lasts for 1 hour. \n<color=#354252>7. Reward Distribution by Presidents</color> \nDays 7–8 are reserved for Presidents to distribute battle spoils to their alliances. \n<color=#354252>8. Reward Distribution by Alliances</color>\nOn Days 9–10, R4/R5 distribute spoils to outstanding alliance members.
915190=1. Matched states are grouped by the system based on overall strength, with Attackers and Defenders assigned accordingly. \n2. Each camp starts with a base pool of spoils, which can be expanded through specific in-game actions. \n3. During the Invitation phase, you may negotiate with unaligned states by offering post-combat spoil shares, persuading them to join your camp. \n4. Spoil distribution is safeguarded by the system. Once partnership and distribution ratios are confirmed, they will be enforced automatically. \n5. During the Combat Phase, states within the same camp must teleport to the designated Defender State to compete for control of building and ore resources. \n6. When the combat begins, all headquarters inside the combat area will be relocated outside the battlefield. Survivors must teleport again to re-enter the combat area. \n7. Throughout the combat, survivors can earn Camp Points via specific actions. When the combat time's up, the camp with the higher total points wins. \n8. Spoils are distributed during the Reward Distribution phase, and each survivor may claim only one share.

915196=<color=#354252>State Selection</color> \nThe Volcano War will commence within the Defender's state. \n\n<color=#354252>Hard Mode</color> \n1. Defenders can opt for the Hard Mode during the Comms phase. \n2. Choosing it prevents inviting partners, and the Attackers may come from up to 3 States. \n3. In Hard Mode, the Defender receives a powerful combat buff. \n\n<color=#354252>Invitation Rules</color> \n1. During the Invitation phase, each state may invite only one other state at a time. \n2. Invitations last for 1 hour. No response in 1 hour equals rejection. \n\n<color=#354252>Distributable Rewards</color> \nEach camp starts with a base pool of distributable rewards. The reward pool size can be boosted through the following actions: \n1. Successfully inviting a state to join during the Invitation phase. \n2. Defenders choosing Hard Mode. \n3. Winning the battle. \n\nStates assigned during the System Allocation phase do not add rewards to the pool and are not eligible for reward distribution. \n\n<color=#354252>Areas</color> \n1. Areas closer to the volcanic core area spawn higher-quality resource deposits. \n2. Teleportation is not allowed in the volcanic core area, and Peace Shield cannot be activated in the volcanic central area. \n\n<color=#354252>Battle Outcome</color> \n1. After the combat time's up, the server determines the winner based on the total camp points.\n\n<color=#354252>Teleportation Rules</color> \n1. Only survivors with Headquarters Lv.15 or higher may teleport into the volcanic area. \n2. Cross-state teleporting cooldowns are shared between this event and State Duel. \n3. After the battle starts, teleporting into the volcanic area from outside does not consume Teleporters. \n4. Teleporting within the volcanic area is free after the battle starts, with a 5-minute cooldown.

915513=1. The event is held every Wednesday at 00:10, 08:10, and 16:10 (Apocalypse Time), each session lasting for 50 mins. \n2. After the first session of the event day (00:10), Night Countesses will appear in the top 3 highest-level neutral cities captured by each alliance (excluding the Capital). \n3. Alliance members must team up to slay the Countesses. \n4. A Night Countess slain during a session of the event day will not reappear in the following sessions. If not killed, she will reappear in the next session. \n5. Neutral cities where the Night Countesses appear are cursed, reducing their buffs (including capture buffs, alliance stone production speed, and season point growth). \n6. Each Night Countess spawn adds 1 stack of curse; max 3 stacks per neutral city. \n7. After slaying the Night Countess, all curses on that neutral city are removed. Captured cities cannot be declared war on by other alliances during the event. \n9. 915579=Night Ritual
915580=1. The event is held every Monday at 00:10, 08:10, 16:10 (Apocalypse Time), each session lasting for 50 mins.\n2. When the event starts, Night Altars will randomly appear in the world. All survivors must destroy the altars to obtain rewards. \n3. Attacking an altar consists of two phases. Phase 1: Survivors send troops to attack 3 Night Priests around each altar. After all 3 are defeated, Phase 2 begins. Phase 2: Survivors must team up to attack the Night Gargoyle. \n4. Whenever HP of Night Priests & the Night Gargoyle is reduced by a certain amount, several Ritual Chests drop around them. Survivors can claim these chests for rewards. \n5. Each Ritual Chest can be claimed up to 5 times, and each survivor can only claim it once. Claimed chests can be shared in the chat channel so other survivors can claim them. Each survivor can claim up to 10 Ritual Chests per day. \n6. Each Ritual Chest has a time limit. Once the countdown ends, any unclaimed chests disappear. \n7. After each event day ends, rewards will be sent via mail based on the Total DMG rankings against the Night Priests & Night Gargoyle. Both DMG rankings will be cleared when the next event day begins.

922001=Endless Night Duke
922002=Background: \n\n1. The Endless Night Duke is the oldest and most terrifying existence in this world. In the long-lost bygone era, he wielded darkness as his reins and blood as his whip, ruling over the order of the world, as well as life and death itself. \n2. Over the long years, invincible solitude and boredom gnawed at his will. Eventually, he chose to slumber in the underground palace he had built himself. A millennium passed, and the old order crumbled during his sleep; even his name was buried by dust and mist.\n3. Yet, the clamor of human warfare ultimately pierced the silence of the underground palace. He did not get angry; instead, upon waking, he sensed the presence of new prey. This long-missed amusement compelled him to open his scarlet eyes once more and personally forge his own new dark age. \n\n\nEvent Rules: \n\n1. The Endless Night Duke event begins in the 4th week of the season and lasts for 7 weeks.\n2. After the event starts, from 00:00 on Saturday to 00:00 on the following Thursday (server time), it is the Silver Ingot Donation Phase. Survivors need to donate Silver Ingots obtained from various events to the Capital, working together to forge a "Silver Artifact." The Silver Artifact can effectively counter the Endless Night Duke and weaken his power.\n3. The Endless Night Duke will appear on Friday server time. The President can choose one of three time slots to gather the strength of the server's survivors to confront the Endless Night Duke.\n4. In the battle against the Endless Night Duke, you can earn ranking reward based on your damage ranking. After the battle against the Endless Night Duke ends, regardless of whether your State defeats him, six Large Steel Plants will appear around the Capital. Dispatching troops to gather will yield a large amount of Steel.\n5. If your State defeats him ahead of schedule, all survivors who dealt damage to the Endless Night Duke will receive a special Victory Reward. If the Silver Artifact was previously activated, the Victory Reward will be doubled!\n6. Remember! The Endless Night Duke grows stronger over time. Survivors must race against time to defeat him completely before he evolves into his final form! Only then can the endless night curse be truly ended.

5730148=Battle of Victory
5730149=Surrender of Helmets
5730150=Long ago, the Obsidian Valley suffered years of relentless drought. The villagers fed on bitter roots, and not one child had ever seen a ripened grain. One evening at dusk, the seven-colored clouds parted, and Quetzalcoatl descended in a spiral, his wings like winds adorned with stars. Upon the cracked earth, he opened the Casket of Sunwheel Corn Seeds, and filled an obsidian water jug, etched with rain patterns, with the very first drop of rain. He told the people, "Bury the seeds in the soil and wait with patience; the sun and the rain shall become your friends." Kneeling in the mud, they understood the rhythm of the seasons for the first time.
5730151=The next day, Quetzalcoatl walked across the hillsides with a crescent-shaped planting staff, demonstrating how to turn the soil, dig holes, cover the seeds, and protect the sprouts with withered leaves. A humble farmer, hands stained with dirt, followed closely behind, teaching every step to his neighbors. He wore no grand crown, only a worn-out robe and a basket filled with seeds. At first, the seeds remained silent, and the villagers nearly gave up; but when the first tender leaf finally pierced the soil, Quetzalcoatl taught them to read the leaf veins and ward off pests. Elders and children joined the labor, and finally the valley was covered in orderly green.
5730152=When the rainy season arrived, torrential storms washed away the new sprouts, and the dry-season springs could not reach the distant fields. Quetzalcoatl thrust a jade feather into the stream, and the water instantly began to churn with thunder-patterned, twin-wheel waterwheels. Copper leaves on the wheels scooped up the spring water, pouring it into jade lifting buckets, carrying it to the higher terraces. The people learned to adjust the wheels by the wind and swap the buckets by the water level; the rhythmic clicking of the axles became their new agricultural clock. Months later, the fields were neither flooded nor cracked. As the corn stalks grew, they rustled in the wind, as if the valley itself was breathing in harmony with the divine.
5730153=On the eve of the harvest, Quetzalcoatl told the villagers: Corn must not only be planted, but also stored, traded, and shared. Pointing to the basalt city gates soon to be built, he taught them to plan the streets, granaries, and plazas aligned with the sunwheel. In the center of the fields, they found a colossal stalk of corn, taller than any adult, with golden kernels shining like jewels under the sunlight. They placed it at the heart of the city as a symbol of abundance and harvest. Stone walls rose layer by layer, embedded with carvings of water waves, feathered patterns, and grains. Viewed from above, the city resembled an opened corn husk. The new city finally received its name-Corn City.
5730154=On the day Corn City was completed, five granaries were filled with golden ears of corn, and the people pushed harvest carts decorated with sun feathers through the city gates. The carts carried the fullest corn, colorful fabrics, and precious gems, while golden wheels left trails of light like scattered grains along the streets. As night fell, people lit bonfires, and Quetzalcoatl spread his colorful wings atop the walls, protecting every warm household light. The golden harvest altar held the first bowl of corn porridge, and the elders offered their gratitude: "You taught us not only how to farm, but also how to live together." Quetzalcoatl ascended into the sky as the morning mist, and the prosperous days of Corn City continued year after year, forevermore.
